items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He had come to Europe in 1947 with a group that included Sandy Williams... Don Gais, piano...

ctx.x: Eventually, I ran into "Big Boy" Goddie, who had spent the 2nd world war years in South America. I also later saw Arthur Briggs, who had been in a concentration camp after the Germans occupied Paris. Briggs told me why the few of the old gang that was still in Parid did not hang around in Boudon's anymore. The owner had collaborated with the Germans, and had denounced some Jews and Negros. I had been eating in the place, but went somewhere else after hearing what Briggs told me.

I heard that Rex Stewart was in Paris, but didn't see him until two weeks had passed as I didn't know where he was living, I happened to be sitting at the Omnibus café at Place Pigalle, and Rex came alone. He had come to Europe in 1947 with a group that included Sandy Williams, ex-Chick Webb trombonist, Vernon Story, a tenor sax man. Don Gais, piano, Johnny Harris, alto and clarinet, Ted Curry, drums and Honey Johnson, a vocalist. He used an unknown French bassist.

It seemed like old times seeing Rex, whom I had not seen for quite a long time. He gave me his address which was on rue Washington near Champ Elysees, and invited me to dinner. While in Paris, he was going to a cooking school and said that he would let me know when I should come to his placefor dinner.
